precepts.text: The coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them, so Dan went up to fight against Leshem and took it; this campaign against Laish is that history.
precepts.point: The children of Dan sent five men of valour from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out land to conquer, and on their way they came to mount Ephraim and lodged at the house of Micah.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why:
“unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes of Israel.” Dan had conquered in Joshua’s day but never attained all their land. “And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.”

This campaign against Laish is that history. The five men of valour sent from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out the land and search it were the beginning of it, in those days when there was no king in Israel.

precepts.text: Simeon's inheritance is named, Beersheba, and Sheba, and Moladah, and the cities round about.
precepts.point: Their dwellings at Beersheba and the surrounding cities are named, the same inheritance given to Simeon in Joshua.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 4: The Families of Judah and Simeon

precepts.why:
“And they had in their inheritance Beer–sheba, Sheba, and Moladah,” and the cities round about. These are Simeon's inheritance in Joshua, the same dwellings Chronicles names: “they dwelt at Beer–sheba, and Moladah”, and the rest. “These were their cities unto the reign of David.”

Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, “but his brethren had not many children, neither did all their family multiply, like to the children of Judah.” Simeon kept its inheritance, but the blessing of increase rested on Judah.

precepts.text: The children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, took it, and called it Dan after the name of their father.
precepts.point: Huram promised to cut wood out of Lebanon as much as Solomon needed and bring it in floats by sea to Joppa, from where it would be carried up to Jerusalem. These floats are like the large cargo ships and barges seen today upon the rivers and the seas.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.”

Leshem is Laish, the same city. Joshua and Judges together show how a city named Dan came to stand within the borders of Naphtali, and why Huram's mother is called “of the daughters of Dan” in Chronicles and “of the tribe of Naphtali” in Kings.

points: The second lot came forth to Simeon, and their inheritance was within the inheritance of the children of Judah.

On the map the whole land Judah possessed is marked as one, and within it sits the portion where Simeon resided, down by Beer-sheba. The so-called Dominicans, of Simeon, were living within the land of the so-called African Americans, of Judah; this is our history and where we lived.
It only sounds crazy because we are not taught anything prior to 1492; we are the real Jews, and these maps show where our forefathers and our foremothers were living.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families, out of the portion of the children of Judah: for the part of the children of Judah was too much for them.
Judah had a lot of area and was being his brother's keeper: come dwell with us, Simeon, we got you; therefore the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their families, and the border of their inheritance was unto Sarid, twelve cities with their villages.

Zebulun sat north, together with Issachar and Asher; those three tribes would always reside together, just like today, and Naphtali stayed close to Asher. The same way, Reuben and Gad were always together on the map.

Today Gad and Reuben reside in the United States of America: Reubenites in Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, Louisiana, and Oklahoma, and Gad also in Idaho, North Dakota, South Dakota, Utah, Texas, and New Mexico; they are known today as the North American Indians or First Nations peoples, but according to the Bible they are Israelites.

Seminole is not a real nationality; seminole means runaway, and Indian goes into slave or servant. God calls you Reuben, God calls you Israel; the Most High gave you a holy, sanctified, powerful name. We are the twelve tribes, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The fourth lot came out to Issachar according to their families, and their border was toward Jezreel; their coast reached to Tabor and went out at Jordan, sixteen cities with their villages.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families; their border reached to Carmel westward, up to great Zidon and to the strong city Tyre, twenty and two cities with their villages.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The sixth lot came out to the children of Naphtali; their coast reached to Zebulun on the south side, to Asher on the west side, and to Judah upon Jordan toward the sunrising, meaning the east.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The fenced cities are cities with great walls; they were bordered and protected for military purposes, so that the land and the city would not be infiltrated.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families, with Zorah, Eshtaol, Ajalon, Ekron, and the border before Japho.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: they lost their portion, they let it slip, and they had to go and conquer different territory.

Therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, took it, smote it with the edge of the sword, possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: When they had made an end of dividing the land, the children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun according to the word of the Lord: the city which he asked, Timnath-serah in mount Ephraim; and he built the city and dwelt therein.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes divided the inheritances by lot in Shiloh before the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. So they made an end of dividing the country; everybody had their portion, and everyone was satisfied.
